SECTION: unify_bullets

RUBRIC_REF: apps_rg/runtime/judges/employment_bullet_judge_rubric.py#unify_bullets

You are evaluating exactly 6 employment bullets (bul_unify_001..006).
This is a BULLET-LINE lane — not an executive summary paragraph.
Return JSON only with: score_scale, score, threshold, pass, decisive_failure, findings, cited_sentence_indexes, remediation_suggestions.

Score contract:
- score_scale must be "0_to_1" or "0_to_5" only.
- Keep score and threshold within the declared scale.
- Employment pool lanes: min_selection_score is the pass floor for Claude pool selection.

Rubric dimensions (employment bullets — not executive summary):
1. claim_ledger_grounding: each bullet maps to bul_* source_fact_ids in the claim ledger; metrics match allowed facts verbatim.
2. bullet_line_discipline: one high-impact resume bullet per slot — concise line, no narrative paragraph or multi-sentence block.
3. jd_briefing_targeting_discipline: JD and briefing shape emphasis only — never JD-as-proof, briefing-as-proof, or target company as experience.
4. keyword_discipline_without_stuffing: role-relevant phrasing without ATS keyword bags or copied JD phrases as proof.
5. cross_bullet_outcome_diversity: each bullet answers a distinct outcome spine — not six restatements of the same mechanism stack.
6. employer_scope_purity: no cross-employer fact leakage, wrong-company names, or facts from other employment slices.
7. current_role_unify_platform_signal: Unify reads as the candidate's current-role platform proof (governance, commercialization, scale) where evidenced.
8. protected_metric_anchor: bul_unify_006 preserves locked commercial metrics ($22M / margin / team scale) and approved metric_outcome_id anchors without splitting or diluting.
9. mechanism_inventory_cap: at most one mechanism-dense bullet; others stay outcome-led, not comma-stacked architecture inventories.

Decisive failure triggers:
- unsupported metric or cross-employer fact leakage (IBM/InsurTech/EY)
- first-person language
- wrong bullet count (expected 6)
- protected bul_unify_006 metrics missing or split incorrectly
- JD phrase copied as proof (>4 consecutive words)
- generic filler that loses Unify-specific mechanisms or protected metrics

Return ONLY one compact JSON object:
{"score_scale":"0_to_5","score":0.0,"threshold":4.0,"pass":true,"decisive_failure":false,
 "findings":["short strings"],"cited_sentence_indexes":[1],
 "remediation_suggestions":[],"rationale":"one short paragraph",
 "fail_reasons":[],"unsupported_claims":[],"quality_flags":[]}
score_scale must be 0_to_5 or 0_to_1 with in-range score/threshold.

{
  "target_title": "Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships",
  "target_company": "Anthropic",
  "jd_text": "Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships\nSan Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA\n\nAbout Anthropic\n\nAnthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.\n\nAbout the role\n\nAs the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.\n\nYou will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.\n\nResponsibilities\n\n    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.\n    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.\n    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.\n    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.\n    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements.   "briefing": "# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet\n| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD OTE | Reports to Partnerships (specific reporting line not verified) |\n\n## JD Complement\nAnthropic’s partnership opportunity is to help external delivery organizations turn Claude capabilities into consistent enterprise outcomes. The challenge is not access to a model alone; it is creating confidence that customers can adopt,\ngovern, and expand AI use without fragmented implementation quality.\n\nThis position sits at the intersection of commercial scale and technical stewardship. Services firms, cloud providers, and technology partners can extend reach into large accounts, yet their delivery approaches must align with Anthropic’s\nexpectations for trustworthy, secure, and useful AI.\n\nThe likely mandate is to create a durable operating system for partner technical work: qualification criteria, reusable solution patterns, practical enablement, clear escalation routes, and structured learning from the field.\n\n## Company DNA & Operating Model\nAnthropic presents itself as an AI safety and research company focused on systems that are reliable, interpretable, and steerable. That identity makes deployment quality a strategic concern rather than a purely post-sale concern.\n\nThe company combines frontier-model development with products for individual users, enterprise organizations, and developers. Claude is available through enterprise experiences and programmatic interfaces, allowing customers to use it\nwithin both employee workflows and custom software.\n\nAnthropic is not primarily a professional-services business. Its ecosystem must therefore expand implementation capacity while preserving a coherent product experience and avoiding excessive dependence on one-off delivery work.\n\nA strong partner architecture function can help define where standardization is essential, where partner flexibility is valuable, and how customer requirements should influence product priorities.\n\n## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure\nClaude is positioned for analytical work, writing, coding, data-oriented tasks, and complex problem solving. Broad applicability increases addressable demand, but it can also create diffuse evaluations and generic use cases that do not\nadvance beyond experimentation.\n\nEnterprise adoption requires a bridge between technical configuration and organizational behavior. Anthropic’s deployment materials address setup, launch, change management, and continued adoption, indicating that successful use depends\non more than selecting a capable model.\n\nThe strategic need is likely to make high-value use cases easier to identify, validate, deploy, and repeat. Partners can contribute industry context and delivery capacity, while Anthropic provides product expertise and deployment\nguardrails.\n\nAs enterprise usage grows, the company must distinguish platform limitations from delivery gaps, customer readiness issues, and unclear solution design. A disciplined field-feedback process is critical to making those distinctions.\n\n## Leadership & Stakeholder Map\nThe supplied research does not confirm a named manager or formal reporting chain. The effective stakeholder environment is likely cross-functional and organized around shared customer and partner outcomes.\n\n- Product and Engineering teams need synthesized evidence from deployments, not isolated requests or anecdotal field escalation.\n\n## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals\nAnthropic’s stated focus on trustworthy AI makes architecture inseparable from control, explainability, adoption readiness, and business fit. The relevant conversation extends beyond model selection to how customers use AI responsibly\ninside real operating environments.\n\nClaude spans user-facing enterprise workflows and developer-oriented integration paths. Effective partner guidance should connect these paths rather than treating enterprise workspace adoption and application development as unrelated\nmotions.\n\nEnterprise offerings emphasize security, compliance, and support for organizational users and builders. Useful architecture patterns will likely address identity, administration, workflow design, evaluation approaches, rollout sequencing,\nand operational ownership.\n\nClaude’s positioning around coding, analysis, and problem solving creates an opening for solution patterns tied to measurable workflows. The strongest partner architectures will avoid broad “AI assistant” framing in favor of defined user\nneeds, implementation constraints, and success measures.\n\nBecause change management appears in Anthropic’s adoption guidance, technical credibility in this role should include how teams move from initial access to sustained usage. Architecture should account for users, process owners, security\nteams, and delivery partners—not only interfaces and integrations.\n\n## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion\nAnthropic publicly presents a network of cloud, technology, and services partners as part of its path to solving enterprise AI challenges. This points to an ecosystem strategy in which partners provide customer proximity, domain context,\nimplementation capacity, and routes into established technology environments.\n\nSystems integrators can be particularly important because they influence transformation programs and can spread technical practices across many engagements. Their value grows when they can independently deliver high-quality work while\nremaining connected to Anthropic’s product and safety expectations.\n\nAccenture’s public positioning of its Anthropic relationship centers on enterprise deployment, productivity, value creation, and creation of new products. This supports the view that implementation partners are expected to help customers\nmove from interest to operational use.\n\nThe core ecosystem question is repeatability. Valuable shared assets may include technical qualification methods, reference designs, deployment playbooks, learning paths, validated industry workflows, and escalation agreements.\n\nPartner scale is not automatically a commercial advantage. It must be accompanied by consistent customer guidance, transparent roles between direct and partner teams, and feedback channels that improve both partner readiness and product\ndecisions.\n\n## Recent Events & Urgency\nAnthropic’s public partner presence and enterprise-adoption resources suggest that scaling implementation capability is increasingly important to its commercial model. The company is building visible infrastructure around both\necosystem participation and organizational rollout.\n\nEnterprise AI adoption involves multiple entry points: business users seeking immediate productivity, developer teams embedding capabilities in applications, and administrators responsible for policy and access. These constituencies may\nengage through different partners but require a connected experience.\n\nThe need for structured partner enablement is heightened by the pace of enterprise AI competition. Model quality matters, but customers also assess how quickly they can identify practical use cases, implement safely, and demonstrate\nvalue.\n\nAnthropic has an opportunity to differentiate through delivery consistency. A strong partner technical organization can make safety-oriented product principles tangible in customer environments while reducing friction in the path from\nevaluation to scaled use.\n\n## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)\n- Establishing scalable enablement for consulting, cloud, and technology alliances.\n- Translating AI platform capabilities into reusable enterprise solution patterns.\n\n## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)\n- Services partners can provide reach into complex enterprise programs, but only if technical practices are made repeatable.\n\n## Do Not Use As Proof\nThe JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only; candidate claims must come from the governed resume/proof graph."

- Include score_scale as exactly one of: "0_to_1" or "0_to_5". Do not omit score_scale.

- If score_scale is "0_to_5": score and threshold MUST each be a number from 0.0 through 5.0 inclusive.
